subject: TTFT & streaming SLOs - follow-up and next steps
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
To: Alice Zhang <alice@acme-corp.com>
Cc: Dylan Brooks <dylan_brooks@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 24 Jun 2026 16:10:00 -0700
Subject: TTFT & streaming SLOs - follow-up and next steps

Hi Alice (and team),

Thanks again for the call today — great discussion and useful context. Recapping the perf/SLO items we covered and proposed next steps so we have an aligned plan: 

Summary of requirements you shared:
- TTFT target: 150ms avg, p95 <= 300ms for completed first-token across the visible set of request sizes
- Throughput/scale: steady-state ~450 qps per region, peak bursts up to ~1.2k concurrent requests
- Concurrency: goal to sustain 600 concurrent streaming sessions with graceful degradation above that
- Streaming: SSE preferred for web clients; WebSocket for mobile (both required). Chunk cadence goal: ~200-300ms between message chunks (real-time feel) with max chunk sizes of ~2-4 KB payloads
- Fallback behavior: when capacity constrained, small partial-response (first chunk) within 300ms and then queued tokens with progressive delivery

What Redwood will validate/provide:
1) End-to-end TTFT measurement (client-visible first token) vs token-level scheduler timing — we’ll provide both metrics and clarify any differences
2) A perf test harness simulating your QPS + streaming cadence (we'll share scope doc PDF and a sample QPS CSV)
3) Dedicated cluster run with the model variant you specify (we recommend a quantized variant for lower latency)
4) Suggested batch/concurrency config and SSE chunking parameters (we'll propose values, then iterate)

Proposed next steps / ask of Acme:
- Confirm the model family / approximate request size distribution (tokens in/out) so we can size the dedicated job
- Share a sample of your request/response traces (if possible) or confirm we can replay the QPS profile we attach
- Availability for a 2-hour dedicated perf run the week of Jun 29 — please suggest preferred days/times

I’ve attached the perf-harness-scope.pdf and a sample qps-profile.csv for your review. Once you confirm model family and availability we’ll schedule a test, spin up dedicated capacity, and run three ramped passes (cold start, warmed, and sustained steady-state) and share detailed telemetry including TTFT p50/p95/p99, per-chunk cadence, and CPU/GPU utilization.

Thanks — looking forward to validating this with you.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
marissa@redwood.ai | +1 (650) 555-0198

Attachments: perf-harness-scope.pdf, qps-profile.csv
From: Alice Zhang <alice@acme-corp.com>

Cc: Acme Platform Team <platform@acme-corp.com>
Date: Wed, 24 Jun 2026 18:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: TTFT & streaming SLOs - follow-up and next steps

Hi Marissa,

Thanks for the clear recap. This matches what we discussed — a couple of clarifications from our side:
- We currently plan to use your hosted endpoint initially for a pilot, but will need Redwood Private for GDPR regions later. For the perf run please mirror our eu/us config.
- SSE on web is preferred, but our mobile team will use WebSockets — we need both to be tested. Mobile clients expect <300ms first-byte on LTE.
- Concurrency: our production peaks are regional; expect up to ~1,200 concurrent sessions per region during promotions. Sustained steady-state is closer to 450 qps as you listed.
- Cold starts: we’d like to see cold-start TTFT numbers (first request after idle) and warm-run numbers. Can you capture instance spin time and model load time separately?

I’ve attached a short CSV with our expected QPS distribution and a sample trace. Please confirm you received the attachments and whether the proposed week of Jun 29 works.

Also — on fallback semantics: if you need to return a partial response quickly and stream the remainder, what guarantees do you expose about ordering and token completeness? We need deterministic assembly on our side.

Thanks,
Alice Zhang
Senior Product Manager, Acme Retail
alice@acme-corp.com

Attachments: acme-qps-profile.csv, acme-sample-trace.json
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
To: Alice Zhang <alice@acme-corp.com>
Cc: Dylan Brooks <dylan_brooks@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 25 Jun 2026 08:15:00 -0700
Subject: Re: TTFT & streaming SLOs - follow-up and next steps

Alice — got the attachments, thanks. Forwarding a proposed test plan and a couple clarifications below.

Proposed perf plan (high level):
- Day 0 (prep): confirm model binary, token budgets, and sample workload. Configure logging (TTFT markers, chunk timestamps).
- Day 1 (cold-start pass): spin up fresh dedicated cluster, run ramp to 50 qps, capture first-request TTFT and model load times.
- Day 1 (warmed passes): after warmup, run 3 sustained passes at your steady-state (450 qps) and one burst to 1.2k concurrent sessions. Capture p50/p95/p99 and chunk cadence metrics.
- Post-run: we’ll deliver a report with E2E TTFT, scheduler-level timings, chunk cadence distribution (ms), and recommended batching/kv-cache configurations.

Responses to your questions:
- We will capture both cold-start model-load timings and E2E first-token latency. We’ll add a specific marker for model load and another at the first-byte emission so you can see both numbers.
- Fallback partial-response ordering: Redwood streaming guarantees in-order chunk delivery over SSE/WebSocket. If we serve a partial first chunk then stream the remainder, chunks are emitted in sequence and include sequence ids so your client can deterministically assemble. We’ll include a sample SSE payload schema in the run artifacts.

Proposed dates: Tue Jun 30 or Wed Jul 1 for the 2-hour dedicated run (both mornings PT). Please confirm which works for you and whether you want the EU region first or US.

We’ll also create a HubSpot record and link (see deal id ACME-347) and upload the perf artifacts to the Drive folder in the related_links above.

Thanks — looping Dylan (infra lead) to set up the dedicated cluster.

Best,
Marissa

My recommendation is to capture both and treat E2E as the primary SLO. Also, I’ll attach the recommended SSE chunking headers and sequence-id schema to the run artifacts.

I’ll schedule infra for Jun 30 morning PT and confirm instance sizing by EOD.
